stories.title: Five takeaways from Burnham's Commons debut as PM
stories.summary: Andy Burnham faced his first PMQs as Prime Minister, being pressed by Kemi Badenoch on defence spending. He also refused to rule out future tax rises and paid tribute to predecessor Keir Starmer.

stories.title: How Burnham got ready to govern with four key moments mapped out
stories.summary: BBC analysis reveals how Andy Burnham prepared to govern, covering his first No. 10 North meeting in July, cabinet appointments, and establishing his core team including Cabinet Secretary Dame Antonia Romeo.

stories.title: Burnham runs Great North Run for homelessness charity
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham ran in the Great North Run wearing a bib with the number 10, running in aid of Changing Lives homelessness charity.

topics.name: Burnham Gov Intelligence
topics.description: Procurement, tech/AI, spending, vendor & priority signals

stories.title: 🏗️ Burnham government strips back procurement rules to put British jobs at heart of £90bn contracts
stories.summary: The government is replacing existing procurement rules to prioritise British jobs and skills across £90bn of public contracts, signalling a major shift in public sector procurement strategy.

stories.title: 🏗️ Firms told to prioritise new jobs over green targets to win public contracts
stories.summary: Burnham will require firms bidding for public contracts to demonstrate job creation rather than meeting green and social value targets, reorienting the government's procurement evaluation criteria.

stories.title: 🤖 Burnham centralises AI policy within his office — cabinet-level AI minister appointed
stories.summary: PM Burnham appointed Kanishka Narayan as the UK's first Cabinet-level AI minister while dismantling DSIT, redistributing its functions across newly named DBIST, DCMS, and the new Office for the PM and Cabinet.

stories.title: 🤖 Greater Manchester emerges as key hub for digital and technology talent
stories.summary: The Places for Growth programme aims to relocate thousands of public sector digital and technology roles outside London, with Greater Manchester positioned as a leading hub.

stories.title: 🤖 Public sector procurement to drive AI innovation — Chancellor signals new approach
stories.summary: Chancellor John Healey signalled that public sector procurement will be explicitly used to drive AI innovation, with government contracts expected to favour AI-enabled solutions.

stories.title: 🏢 UK warned over dangerous reliance on US tech giants for public sector systems
stories.summary: The Open Rights Group (ORG) has written to politicians warning that Britain is leaning too heavily on US firms such as Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Palantir to run core public sector and cloud systems, amid fears of political leverage.

topics.name: Parliament
topics.description: House of Commons, Lords, PMQs, legislation

stories.title: Burnham's PMQs debut shows challenge of delivering new era
stories.summary: Burnham's first Prime Minister's Questions saw Badenoch quiz him on defence spending and future tax rises. Burnham refused to rule out further taxes and acknowledged the scale of inherited challenges.

stories.title: Parliament returns for autumn term — multiple ministerial statements expected
stories.summary: Parliament returned 1 September with new Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband responding to MPs' questions, and multiple urgent questions and ministerial statements filed after the extended summer recess.

stories.title: House of Commons erupts over assisted dying debate
stories.summary: The Commons saw heated exchanges over the assisted dying bill, with PM Burnham having previously indicated that improvement in palliative care was a prerequisite before any assisted dying service could be introduced.

stories.title: Holborn and St Pancras by-election: Labour's to lose — but lose it might
stories.summary: The Guardian reports Labour faces a tough by-election in Holborn and St Pancras, with the party seen as vulnerable despite holding the seat, amid concerns about Burnham government performance in early weeks.

stories.title: TUC conference: Unions demand Burnham crackdown on zero-hours contracts
stories.summary: The Trades Union Congress is pressing the Burnham government to deliver its promised crackdown on zero-hours contracts, a flagship Labour commitment made in opposition.

stories.title: Conservative reshuffle: who's who in Kemi Badenoch's new top team?
stories.summary: Kemi Badenoch reshuffled the Conservative shadow cabinet at the end of August, with The Guardian outlining the key figures in her new team as she positions the party for opposition.

stories.title: Badenoch condemns Reform UK's 'authoritarian' press bans
stories.summary: Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch attacked Reform UK's reported media access restrictions at their annual conference, calling them 'authoritarian' and attempting to differentiate her party from Farage's movement.

stories.title: More public control is the only way to grow UK economy, Burnham tells MPs
stories.summary: As Burnham made his Commons debut as PM, he argued for greater public ownership as central to his economic growth agenda, drawing criticism from Badenoch who called it a return to 1970s policies.

stories.title: Lib Dems win two council by-elections from Labour and Reform UK
stories.summary: The Liberal Democrats captured council seats from Labour in Devon and from Reform UK in Yorkshire, providing a boost to Sir Ed Davey's party and signalling continued growth in its local base.

topics.name: Reform UK
topics.description: Nigel Farage, party news and announcements

stories.title: Reform UK annual conference held in Birmingham — Farage delivers keynote amid scrutiny
stories.summary: Reform UK held its 2026 national conference at the NEC Birmingham (4–5 September), with Farage delivering a keynote and facing scrutiny over an undercover investigation alleging foreign funding law breaches.

stories.title: Reform beset by internal row over Dover and Portsmouth port protests
stories.summary: Reform UK faced internal divisions after masked protesters blockaded Dover port on the final day of the party conference. Farage condemned the actions as 'horrible' but faced criticism over the party's response.

stories.title: Reform 'very confident' £72m donations were legal amid parliamentary investigation
stories.summary: Reform UK said it was 'very confident' its £72m in donations were legal, even as a parliamentary investigation resumed and Rayner warned of retrospective action over party finances.

stories.title: Swinney to cut Scottish health boards from 14 to two and roll out £2 bus fares
stories.summary: First Minister John Swinney announced a dramatic NHS restructuring — reducing health boards from 14 to 2 — alongside a £2 bus fare cap as part of the SNP government's new Programme for Government focused on cost of living.

stories.title: PM Burnham says second Scottish independence referendum remains 'off limits'
stories.summary: Andy Burnham confirmed that a second Scottish independence referendum will not be granted, but BBC analysis noted this declaration may paradoxically boost support for independence.

stories.title: Burnham government ministerial appointments: July 2026 — full list
stories.summary: Key appointments under PM Burnham include John Healey as Chancellor, Ed Miliband as Foreign Secretary, Louise Haigh as First Secretary of State, and Yvette Cooper in a senior cabinet role. Dan Jarvis, Emma Reynolds and others retained as junior ministers.

stories.title: DSIT scrapped — AI and digital governance restructured across departments
stories.summary: Under Burnham's premiership, the Department for Science, Innovation & Technology (DSIT) was abolished. Its functions were redistributed across DBIST, DCMS, and the new Office for the PM and Cabinet housing the first ever Cabinet-level AI minister.

topics.name: Elections & By-elections
topics.description: Upcoming or recent election results, polls

stories.title: Holborn and St Pancras by-election looming — Labour under pressure
stories.summary: A by-election in the safe Labour seat of Holborn and St Pancras is approaching, with The Guardian warning Labour faces a real risk of losing the seat amid early discontent with the Burnham government.

stories.title: Farage wins local by-election as parliamentary investigation resumes
stories.summary: Nigel Farage won a by-election boycotted by major parties — reportedly without attending the declaration — as a parliamentary investigation into his conduct resumed hours after his victory.

stories.title: Lib Dems capture council seats from Labour in Devon and Reform UK in Yorkshire
stories.summary: The Liberal Democrats won two council by-elections, taking a Labour seat in Devon and a Reform UK seat in Yorkshire, continuing their consistent local government growth.

stories.title: House of Lords (Hereditary Peers) Act 2026 — reform next steps under debate
stories.summary: Following passage of the Hereditary Peers Act 2026, constitutional lawyers and peers are debating what comes next in Lords reform, with broad consensus on further steps but no government timetable confirmed.

stories.title: Lords debate AI and essential services in Cybersecurity and Resilience Bill
stories.summary: The House of Lords debated key provisions around AI and essential services in the Cybersecurity and Resilience Bill, with peers raising concerns about accountability and oversight of AI-driven public systems.
